---
title: "How it works"
---

## Everything happens in the browser

When you add a component, R only stores its settings in the map. The
component itself is a small piece of JavaScript that runs in the reader's
browser: it reads the layer's data once, computes the figures for the whole
map, and recomputes the figures for the view each time the map moves. That
is why the components work in static HTML and Quarto documents, without a
Shiny server.

## What counts as "in view"

A polygon counts as in view when any part of it is on screen; a point, when
the point is on screen. Features outside the layer's zoom range are not
counted.

Relying only on what the map has drawn, with MapLibre's
`queryRenderedFeatures()`, is not enough:

- features too small to be drawn at low zoom are missed;
- on the globe projection, some features far from the center are missed,
  and features on the far side of the globe can be returned as if they
  were visible.

So maplore combines both: a feature is in view if it was drawn **or** a
geometric test finds it on screen, and on the globe only features on the
visible side count. For points, the geometric test alone is used. The
counts have been checked against `sf` and against pixel positions at
several zoom levels, with rotation and pitch.

When the layer has a `filter`, only features drawn on screen are counted,
since the geometric test cannot apply the filter. Very small features may
then be missed at low zoom.

## Performance

Updating takes a few milliseconds for hundreds of polygons or a few
thousand points. With 50,000 points, a summary and a ranking together take
about 20 ms with all of them on screen and still update while panning;
searching them takes about 2 ms. If an update takes longer than 25 ms
(around 200,000 points), the components update only when the map stops
moving, so panning stays smooth.

Several components on the same layer share the work of finding the
features in view.

## Limitations

- One numeric column per component.
- The layer's source must be an `sf` object or inline GeoJSON; vector tile
  sources are not supported.
- Shiny proxies and `compare()` widgets are not supported yet.
